newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to repatriate Albanians seeking refuge.
newsitem.headline: Italy to repatriate Albanians seeking refuge.

text.p: Italy said on Thursday it would send back Albanians who had crossed the Adriatic to escape the violence in their homeland.

"If we had to decide with our hearts, of course, we would let these Albanian citizens stay in Italy, but this would mean opening the doors to everyone," government official Giuseppe Mazzitello told reporters in the southern Puglia region.

He said that a group of 29 Albanians, including nine children, who arrived on a boat in the southern port of Otranto on Wednesday would probably be sent by ferry to Durres since the regular route to Vlore had been interrupted.
Some had asked for political asylum.
Italy organised an airlift of 35 people, Italian citizens and foreign reporters, from the southern Albanian port of Vlore earlier this week after rioting there.
Defence Minister Beniamo Andreatta said on Thursday that Italy was drawing up contingency plans to evacuate its citizens from Tirana and other parts of the Balkan state.
He told a parliamentary commission that plans were being drawn up "should this become necessary in the wake of a general state of disorder endangering the safety of our compatriots.
"In any situation where Italian citizens are in danger, our armed forces are obliged to intervene," Andreatta told the defence commission of the lower house.

U.S. military commanders in Germany said they were also drawing up plans to evacuate more than 1,600 Americans resident in Albania, where rebels have seized towns in the south and army forces have advanced to try to quell the insurrection.

Albanian President Sali Berisha, backed by opposition parties, agreed on Thursday to suspend military activity against rebels in the south and to offer an amnesty to any insurgents who surrendered their weapons within two days.

The Italian foreign ministry welcomed the move, saying in a statement that Berisha's dialogue with opposition was a positive development which it hoped would lead to a political solution to Albania's crisis.

Soldiers fought insurgents east of the Adriatic port of Sarande on Wednesday in the first major clash since Albania declared a state of emergency to contain widespread rioting sparked by the collapse of dubious get-rich-quick schemes.
Andreatta said there was no need to send troops to southern Italy, where authorities have stepped up patrols in case of a wave of immigrants trying to make the 40-mile Adriatic crossing.
Finance police said a group of immigrants, believed to be some 20 Albanians, landed near Lecce on Thursday. They avoided capture but left behind a sack of marijuana.
Italy, which briefly occupied Albania during World War Two, has been a magnet in recent years for illegal immigrants seeking to flee Europe's poorest state.
Tens of thousands of Albanians made a mass exodus to Italy in 1991 after 45 years of Stalinist rule crumbled.

Italian officials say there are nearly 64,000 Albanians legally resident but more than 200,000 could be in the country illegally. Italy threw out almost 13,000 Albanians last year and some 900 have been stopped trying to enter this year.
Earlier this week, two Albanian pilots flew their MIG-15 into Italy and asked for political asylum.
